mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strong labor market, which positively impacts consumer confidence and spending, leading to increased corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of the 20-day windows following a UNRATE decline, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) crosses below 4.5%, it indicates monetary easing, which lowers borrowing costs and stimulates investment, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 does not show positive returns in more than 55% of the 20-day windows after FEDFUNDS falls below 4.5%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When both housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) show concurrent growth, it indicates strong consumer demand, which drives corporate revenues and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 35% of the 60-day windows following concurrent growth in HOUST and RSAFS, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) signals increased economic activity, which leads to higher corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of the 20-day windows following an INDPRO increase, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: GDP growth (GDPC1) indicates strong economic activity, which leads to increased consumer and business spending, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 35% of the 60-day windows following GDPC1 growth, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) signals a strong labor market, which leads to increased consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 45% of the 5-day windows following a PAYEMS increase, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 4.5% and GDP growth (GDPC1) is positive, it indicates a stimulative monetary policy environment, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 30% of the 60-day windows following the joint condition, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 5%, it indicates a tightening monetary policy, which increases borrowing costs and reduces investment, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 40% of the 20-day windows following FEDFUNDS exceeding 5%, the hypothesis is rejected.
